rules.source: Law No. 63 of 2015 on Combating Information Technology Crimes (Kuwait) — https://www.coe.int/web/octopus/-/kuwait
rules.retrieved_snippet: Search summary: the Council of Europe country profile lists Law 63/2015 among Kuwaiti laws covering illegal access, data interference and computer-related fraud, noting some offences are not criminalised to the extent the Budapest Convention requires; DLA Piper adds that it penalises illegal dealing with personal or governmental data.

rules.source: Law No. 20 of 2014 on Electronic Transactions (Kuwait) with Decision No. 48 of 2014; CITRA Administrative Decision No. 26 of 2024 (Data Privacy Protection Regulation, telecom licensees only) — https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?c=KW&t=law
rules.retrieved_snippet: DLA Piper (search summary): Kuwait has no dedicated general personal data protection law; Law No. 20 of 2014 includes data privacy provisions for electronic records, and CITRA's 2024 Data Privacy Protection Regulation applies exclusively to CITRA-licensed telecom providers. One other source labels the 2024 instrument a 'law'; legal form unresolved.
